verdict.rationale: Fellow, a meeting-notes SaaS rather than an agent, documents an official MCP server. It lets AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor access meeting notes, action items, transcripts and calendar events, and it works with any connector-capable AI tool. Workspace owners can enable it, revoke connections and see last-used timestamps, and access is scoped to each user's existing permissions; a probe confirms the official MCP doc page exists. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of connecting an agent, and documented connection/auth setup details and an enumerated tool catalog.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: Fellow's MCP server allows you to connect your AI meeting notes, action items, transcripts, calendar events and more, to your favourite AI assistants.
Your favorite AI chatbot like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can now tap directly into your meeting recaps, notes, and action items
Fellow’s MCP Connector works with any AI tool that supports connectors, so you're never locked into one platform
Workspace owners decide when the MCP Server is enabled, can revoke connections at any time, and see the last-used timestamp for every connection
